meta.scope: Five 2026 Week 10 games transcribed in full from the official report (WAS@NYG, NE@DET, KC@ATL, MIN@GB, JAX@TEN). BUF@NYJ was only partially returned and is therefore excluded rather than half-transcribed.
meta.rule: Nothing about who starts, what string a backup is, or who replaces whom is inferred. Those cells are blank until a depth-chart feed is committed.

feeds.feed: Official injury report (weekly, practice + game status)
feeds.useful_for: Who is on the report this week and how much they practised.
feeds.status: available upstream, NOT committed in this repository; release assets are reachable only from a GitHub-hosted runner, not from this sandbox

feeds.feed: Weekly depth chart (pos_rank per position slot, with a `dt` timestamp)
feeds.useful_for: The 1st/2nd/3rd/4th string question. `pos_rank` is the only field that answers it.
feeds.status: available upstream, NOT committed; note the source changed after 2024, so 2015-2024 and 2025-2026 need separate handling

feeds.feed: Snap counts per player per game (offence/defence/ST, % of snaps)
feeds.useful_for: Whether a backup actually played, and how much the role changed week to week.
feeds.status: available upstream, NOT committed; derived from Pro Football Reference, i.e. a third party, not the NFL itself

feeds.feed: Participation (11 personnel groupings, on-field players per play)
feeds.useful_for: Which eleven were actually on the field for each snap - the strongest available check on a lineup claim.

feeds.feed: Schedules with closing lines and prices
feeds.useful_for: Settling any strategy at the closing line.

questions.question: Is a listed starter ruled OUT for a specific game?
questions.answer: Yes, partially: the official report's Game Status column gives Out/Doubtful/Questionable.

questions.question: Is the player who is OUT actually the 1st-string starter at that position?
questions.answer: NOT ANSWERABLE from what is committed. The injury report has no depth rank, and no depth-chart feed is in this repository.

questions.question: Is the replacement the 2nd, 3rd or 4th string?
questions.answer: NOT ANSWERABLE. `pos_rank` in the depth-chart feed is the field that answers this; nothing else in the official feeds ranks backups.

questions.question: Did the replacement actually take the starter's snaps?
questions.answer: NOT ANSWERABLE without snap counts or participation data (F-3/F-4).

questions.question: How much does losing a starter move the line?
questions.answer: NOT MEASURED. This is the central quantitative question and it needs ID-01..ID-04 plus a timestamped line to be answerable.

questions.question: Does the market already price the injury?
questions.answer: UNKNOWN. The committed schedules file has one un-timestamped closing line per game, so the pre-news and post-news prices cannot be separated.

questions.question: When must a club file its practice report?
questions.answer: Thursday/Friday/Saturday for a Sunday game, by 4:00 p.m. New York time (and the equivalent schedule for other game days); a Game Status Report is due the day before the game. The league's own calendar states this.

questions.question: Is the report complete at the start of the week?
questions.answer: No. At retrieval on 12 Nov the Game Status column was blank for most players because the game-status report is filed later in the week. A mid-week snapshot is not a final availability list.

irregularities.title: Injury, depth and snap feeds are not in the repository
irregularities.detail: The upstream releases exist for every season 2009-2026 (injuries), 2001-2026 (depth charts) and 2012-2026 (snap counts), but none is committed here and the release assets redirect to a host this sandbox cannot reach.
irregularities.needs: Run the download on a GitHub-hosted runner and commit derived summaries.

irregularities.title: The depth-chart source changed after the 2024 season
irregularities.detail: nflreadr's data dictionary states the source changed after 2024; the 2025+ fields are dt/team/player_name/pos_grp_id/pos_grp/pos_id/pos_name/pos_abb/pos_slot/pos_rank. Any history built across that boundary mixes two schemas.
irregularities.needs: Treat 2015-2024 and 2025-2026 as separate regimes, or normalise only on pos_rank.

irregularities.title: Snap counts come from Pro Football Reference, not the NFL
irregularities.detail: nflreadr's loader for snap counts describes the source as Pro Football Reference, a third party. It is a strong feed, but it is not an official league source, so a claim resting only on it is 'third-party verified', not 'officially verified'.
irregularities.needs: Label it that way wherever it is used.

irregularities.title: A mid-week report is not a final availability list
irregularities.detail: At retrieval (12 Nov) only a handful of players carried a game status; the rest were practice participation only. Betting on a mid-week snapshot is betting on information that will change before kickoff.
irregularities.needs: Snapshot at the game-status deadline, and store the timestamp with the row.

irregularities.title: The injury page's records are ahead of the committed results extract
irregularities.detail: The official Week 10 page shows NYG 5-2-1 and WAS 2-5-1; the committed extract ends 2026-11-01 and resolves those teams to 4-2-1 and 2-4-1 under its own win convention. The extract is simply older; it is not wrong.
irregularities.needs: Refresh the extract before any analysis that claims to be current.
irregularities.source_text: records printed beside each team on the injury page

irregularities.title: Wins counted by the extract can differ from an official W-L-T record by one
irregularities.detail: KC's official roster page shows 6-2-0 for 2026 while the committed extract, counted through 2026-11-01 by 'margin > 0', gives 5-2. The gap is a tie counted as not-a-win, exactly the convention logged as IR-04 on the verification page. Any win-based feature should therefore be built from an explicit tie convention.
irregularities.needs: Use result > 0 / = 0 / < 0 explicitly and document it.
